Optimal.Notes: A 6 W TDP is more than enough for a locked 60 fps in this 2D game; all visual effects can be left on with no performance cost. This is the recommended everyday profile for comfortable handheld play.

profiles.Summary: Don't Starve is a lightweight 2D indie survival game from 2013 with very modest PC requirements, and it runs excellently on the Steam Deck under Proton with a platinum ProtonDB rating. The game's low hardware demands mean the Deck can run it at full 60 fps with a very low TDP, making it a great battery-friendly title.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very modest 2013 PC minimum requirements and its 2D engine. On your first run, verify that the frame rate holds at 60 fps in busy world areas and that the controller UI is comfortable — if any stuttering occurs, drop to the Max Battery 30 fps cap.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 4 W TDP and a locked 30 fps the Deck barely breaks a sweat on this 2D title; Integer scaling keeps the pixel-art crisp at native resolution. In-game option names are estimated from typical Klei game menus as no Deck-specific guide was available.

MaxPerformance.Notes: This 2D game is so light that 'Max Performance' offers no meaningful visual uplift over Optimal; the uncapped frame rate and auto GPU clock are purely for those who want zero overhead. Consider using the Optimal profile instead for better battery life with identical visuals.

Optimal.Notes: A stable 60 fps at native resolution is easily achievable with minimal power draw; this is the sweet spot for Don't Starve on the Deck. Integer scaling preserves the hand-drawn art style cleanly.
